title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 5 close: unjust acceptio vs liberal gift; Matthew 20:15
pass_a_gloss: To these things; unjust acceptation of persons has no place where someone from mere liberality of his own gives unequally to equals, but where, in the dispensing of things owed, someone favors one before another from regard to some circumstance of the person which is outside the cause of merit: as if a Prelate in the conferring of a benefice should prefer a rich man or his kinsman to more learned and better men, he is an acceptor of persons, because he regards circumstances which do nothing toward the merit or dignity of such a prize. But now God electing one to the kingdom of glory before another does not act from a debt of justice, but from a gift of munificence: nor does he regard nobility, riches, talent, or any other quality whatever outside the matter from which the name of persons is found; but his liberality and goodness, according to that, Matthew 20:15. Is it lawful for me to do what I will with my own? See Augustine, Epistle 106, and On the Good of Perseverance book 2 chapter 8. And against the two Epistles of the Pelagians chapter 3 book 2.
pass_b_english: Further: unjust respect of persons has no place where someone from mere liberality gives unequally of what is his own to equals — only where, in dispensing what is owed, he favors one over another for a personal circumstance outside the cause of merit (as when a prelate, conferring a benefice, prefers a rich man or kinsman to better and more learned men: that is respect of persons, because those circumstances do nothing for the merit or dignity of such a prize). God electing one to the kingdom of glory ahead of another does not act from a debt of justice but from a gift of munificence; he does not regard nobility, riches, talent, or any quality outside the matter that earns the name "respect of persons," but his own liberality and goodness — Matthew 20:15: Is it lawful for me to do what I will with my own? See Augustine, Ep. 106; De bono persever. 2.8; Contra 2 Epist. Pelag. 2.3.
source_text: Ad haec; injusta personarum acceptio locum non habet, ubi quis ex mera liberalitate de suo dat inaequaliter aequalibus, sed ubi, in dispensatione rerum debitarum, quis uni faveat prae altero, ex respectu ad aliquam personae circumstantiam quae est extra causam meriti: ut si Praelatus in collatione beneficii praeferat divitem aut consanguineum suum doctoribus et melioribus viris, est personarum acceptor, quia respicit circumstantias, quae nihil faciunt ad meritum vel dignitatem talis praemii. Jam vero Deus eligens ad regnum gloriae unum prae alio, non agit ex debito justitiae, sed ex dono munificentiae: neque respicit nobilitatem, divitias, ingenium, aut aliam qualitatem quamcunque extra rem, unde personarum nomen invenit; sed liberalitatem et bonitatem suam, juxta illud, Matth. xx. 15. Licet mihi quod volo facere de eo. Videte Augustinum, Epist. 106. et De bono persever. lib. 2. cap. 8. Et contr. 2. Epist. Pelag. cap. 3. lib. 2.
